status: Completed author review of the adult bedside card and its scored form.

sources.section: Gaza MOH injectable medicines guide, p. 78
sources.scope: Continuous IV pump administration. D5W dilution applies to the listed concentrate.
Indication, product-specific preparation, BP and organ perfusion, extravasation ischemia, taper, alpha and beta actions.
Usual first-line norepinephrine. Either norepinephrine or epinephrine may be considered with concomitant cardiac dysfunction. Conditional initial peripheral use when needed to avoid delay.

Continuous pump infusion, site surveillance and taper. MSF expresses the specific preparation and dosage in tartrate units. Its diluents and salt-based dosing must not be transferred to a different product.
Stop infusion, retain cannula for aspiration, avoid flushing, escalate and consider alternate access. Corroborating reference without evidence of local adoption.

facts.rationale: Identify both the pharmacologic class and primary clinical role.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Alpha1-mediated vasoconstriction with some beta1 cardiac stimulation.
facts.rationale: Distinguish alpha1 vascular effects from beta1 cardiac effects.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Strong vasoconstriction raises systemic vascular resistance/MAP
facts.rationale: Connect vasoconstriction with raised vascular resistance and pressure.

facts.sourceExcerpt: For shock, infuse IV continuously on a pump. Verify the exact product, compatible diluent and standard concentration.
facts.rationale: Select compatible dilution of the concentrate and continuous IV pump delivery.

facts.sourceExcerpt: A suitable peripheral IV can be used to start urgent treatment when central access would delay it. Follow the facility protocol for site checks and transition to central access.
facts.rationale: Choose prompt peripheral initiation with frequent checks and reassessment of central access under protocol.

facts.sourceExcerpt: For an order in micrograms/min, multiply by 60 and divide by concentration in micrograms/mL to obtain mL/hour.
facts.rationale: Convert dose per minute and verified concentration on the same norepinephrine basis into mL/hour.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Vasopressor for severe hypotension. In adult septic shock, norepinephrine is the usual first-line vasopressor.
facts.rationale: Select the initial agent in a hypotensive adult with septic shock without cardiac dysfunction.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Cardiac dysfunction may change the choice.
facts.rationale: Identify myocardial dysfunction as a specific modifier of first-line selection.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Follow BP and perfusion closely during titration.
facts.rationale: Distinguish target arterial pressure from restoration of peripheral and organ perfusion.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Inspect a peripheral IV frequently for pain, pallor, swelling, coolness or impaired flow.
facts.rationale: Recognize a focal site pattern that warrants assessment for extravasation and identify the risk mechanism.

facts.sourceExcerpt: For suspected extravasation, stop the infusion through that IV, leave the catheter in place and avoid flushing.
facts.rationale: Select all three immediate IV actions based on the local findings.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Escalate immediately for aspiration and treatment per protocol, and coordinate safe alternate access if pressure support is still needed.
facts.rationale: Keep the original line for aspiration and promptly restore pressure support through alternate access under protocol.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Taper as ordered when discontinuing. Abrupt withdrawal can cause marked hypotension.
facts.rationale: Identify immediate hypotension as the reason to taper and reassess BP.
Explain how local norepinephrine exposure can cause ischemia.
A formulary listing documents availability on the list. Current facility stock and product-specific base or salt expression require verification.

facts.sourceExcerpt: PRESSURE drug: vasopressor for severe hypotension/shock.
Check BP, perfusion and the infusion site. Respond immediately to suspected extravasation.
facts.rationale: Duplicates pressure, perfusion and extravasation objectives.
